q: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one _____ bond.
e: Organic compounds contain carbon and hydrogen in which there is at least one C-C or C-H bond. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds. The organic definition used here needs at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond.

q: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms are bonded to each other by _____ bonds.
e: Hydrocarbons are compounds in which carbon and hydrogen atoms are bonded to each other by covalent bonds. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds.

q: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called _____ hydrocarbons.
e: The hydrocarbon compounds that contain only single bonds are called saturated hydrocarbons. Hydrocarbons with only carbon-carbon single bonds are saturated. Hydrocarbons contain only carbon and hydrogen, joined by covalent bonds. Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.

q: Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes, alkynes and _____ compounds.
e: Unsaturated hydrocarbons include alkenes, alkynes and aromatic compounds. Unsaturated hydrocarbons have a carbon-carbon double or triple bond, so alkenes, alkynes and aromatics sit in that group. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n.

q: The _____ formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule.
e: The molecular formula of an organic compound is the actual number of atoms of each element present in a molecule. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. The molecular formula gives the actual number of each kind of atom in one molecule. Molecular is the word this version is asking about.

q: A full structural formula shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the _____ geometry of the molecule.
e: A full structural formula shows every bond and atom in what order atoms are attached, but does not portray accurately the three-dimensional geometry of the molecule. A structural formula shows which atoms are attached to which, not just the count of each element. A full structural formula draws every bond and atom so you can see the arrangement.

q: A _____ structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule.
e: A condensed structural formula is a more compact way of drawing the structural formula of a molecule. A structural formula shows which atoms are attached to which, not just the count of each element. A condensed structural formula still shows the order of groups but hides many of the individual bonds. Condensed is the word this version is asking about.

q: A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms that determine the _____ properties of a compound.
e: A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms that determine the chemical properties of a compound. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: An alcohol is an organic compound with a _____ functional group attached to a carbon atom.
e: An alcohol is an organic compound with a hydroxyl functional group attached to a carbon atom. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula _____, where R is an alkyl group.
e: Alcohols can often be represented by the general formula ROH, where R is an alkyl group. An alcohol has an -OH group attached to a saturated carbon. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once. ROH is the word this version is asking about.

q: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same functional group and similar structure and whose structures differ only by the number of _____ units in the main carbon chain.
e: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same functional group and similar structure and whose structures differ only by the number of CH_2 units in the main carbon chain. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule.

q: In a homologous series, as the chain gets longer, the compounds show a _____ change in properties.
e: In a homologous series, as the chain gets longer, the compounds show a gradual change in properties. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2.

q: The general formula is used to represent the _____ of organic compounds.
e: The general formula is used to represent the families of organic compounds. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. A general formula such as CnH2n+2 describes a whole homologous series at once. Families is the word this version is asking about.

q: A full structural formula is also known as a graphic formula or _____ formula.
e: A full structural formula is also known as a graphic formula or displayed formula. A structural formula shows which atoms are attached to which, not just the count of each element. A full structural formula draws every bond and atom so you can see the arrangement.

q: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkene is a carbon-carbon double bond. Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon double bond and the general formula CnH2n. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule. Double is the word this version is asking about.

q: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon _____ bond.
e: The functional group in an alkyne is a carbon-carbon triple bond. Alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons with a carbon-carbon triple bond and the general formula CnH2n-2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule. Triple is the word this version is asking about.

q: An alkane is a compound that _____ functional groups.
e: An alkane is a compound that lacks functional groups. Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds and the general formula CnH2n+2. A functional group is the atom or group that sets the characteristic reactions of an organic molecule. Lacks is the word this version is asking about.

q: The carbon atom is _____ to all organic compounds.
e: The carbon atom is central to all organic compounds. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Central is the word this version is asking about.

q: Organic compounds typically contain other elements in addition to carbon and hydrogen, such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the _____.
e: Organic compounds typically contain other elements in addition to carbon and hydrogen, such as oxygen, nitrogen, sulphur, phosphorus and the halogens. An organic compound has carbon and hydrogen with at least one C-C or C-H covalent bond. Organic chemistry is built on carbon-hydrogen frameworks with covalent bonds.

q: A homologous series is usually listed in order of increasing _____.
e: A homologous series is usually listed in order of increasing size. A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same functional group and a general formula that rises by CH2.
